items.author: Ben
items.title: Rivals buy firms too - buy_corporation joins the scored-utility candidate list
items.design: The symmetry half of BL-628 (whole-firm buyout), and a widening of the BL-202/BL-203 exception in its established shape: deterministic, seeded, scored-utility, a legal verb and never a planner. THE WORK: score buy_corporation in corp_ai.cpp's existing candidate list, capped at one acquisition per evaluation, its price carried in the candidate's spend under the solvency gate so a rival cannot buy itself below its reserve floor. Availability is gated on the target's ownership class, not on the acquirer's cash - the 'never on cash' ruling's shape. Record the grant in the standing rules with its date, as every prior widening is recorded. SAVING UP IS NOT PLANNING, and this item owns the distinction: Ben's Sprint 20 goal wants a corp to accumulate cash toward an acquisition, but a scorer that defers a cheap build today in order to afford a firm tomorrow is edging toward the planner the standing rules forbid. The honest route needs no new machinery - accumulation is EMERGENT when the buy candidate outscores the marginal build, since a tick with no affordable positive candidate simply banks its cash. Whether that actually happens at the authored weights is a measurement, and BL-634 (acquisition viability) is where it is taken.

items.title: The Corporations panel does not fit its column - names cut to one letter, Declare Hostile clipped
items.author: Ben
items.design:
OBSERVED LIVE, 2026-08-26 (BL-633's capture), and pre-existing - BL-633 changed no width and no column count. Five columns carrying 62+62+62+220 px of fixed width do not fit the shell fold-out column (380-460 px by resolution) at 1280x720: the Corporation NAME column collapses to a single letter ('F', 'E', 'C') and the Stance column's 'Declare Hostile' button clips off the right edge as 'De...'. This is BL-449's shape exactly - the surface that shipped clean on a compile AND a 36/36 harness while being unusable - still live in the same panel. THE WORK: re-budget the columns against shell_column_width(disp.x) rather than fixed pixels, and decide whether the stance presses belong in-row at this width at all or behind the row's Selection drill. Note NR-663: expect_no_clipping did NOT catch this, because ImGui SmallButton labels are not instrumented into the overflow ledger - so this needs a real look, not a green row.

SUPERSEDED IN PLACE BY BL-674 (diplomacy by stance), 2026-08-29 - newest-dated wins, and this is recorded rather than quietly applied. BL-674 carries Ben's instruction to DELETE the Reach, Share and Stance columns and group the rows by stance instead, which removes the starvation this item proposed to re-budget: three of the five columns stop existing, so there is no fixed-width budget left to blow. This item's second half - whether the stance presses belong in-row at this width - is answered there too (they move into the row's own action affordance and keep their confirms). Left open rather than closed because Ben owns the close; do not build BL-639 and BL-674 as two changes to one file.

items.author: Ben
items.title: Construction draws materials - in the opening years, and as centres grow
items.design: Ben, 2026-08-26: 'we need those first 20 years of generation to include construction'. MEASURED CONTEXT: materials are authored per building (resource_costs) and charged at the build press, but generation PLACES buildings rather than constructing them, so the draw never fires during the opening years - stone and timber have a construction sink on paper and no pull in practice. TWO HALVES, and the second is the one that lasts: (1) make the opening years actually build, so the warm start carries a real material pull; (2) make POPULATION CENTRES draw construction materials as they grow, which does not decay once the warm start ends. An ancient economy's largest material sink is building, and half (2) makes that structurally true rather than transiently.

items.author: Ben
items.title: Roads, ports and hubs draw materials to stay standing
items.design: The infrastructure demand channel (MARKETS.md section Demand channels). The logistics_maintenance budget line already exists and names exactly this, so the state half has a home. THE WORK: a network that consumes stone and timber to stay standing - a permanent sink scaled by GEOGRAPHY rather than by population, which is a shape none of the other channels has. Second-order and wanted: it gives reach a running cost, so extending the network becomes a decision rather than a ratchet. OWED: this item writes its paragraph into LOGISTICS.md; the design register in MARKETS.md points at it.

items.author: Ben
items.title: Government satellite launches - the tenth budget line, and space goods' first real buyer
items.design: Ben, 2026-08-26: 'add endpoints for space goods in government issued satellite launches'. Design in NATIONS.md section A budget. THE MACHINERY EXISTS - nations hold a weighted budget over priority lines, run_national_budget has claim/transfer machinery, and strategic_reserve is already a goods-buying line that no consumer claims on. THE WORK: a tenth line, space_programme, buying spacecraft_components and propellant through the BL-350 procurement seam (never on the open market - that is strategic_reserve's own rule). APPEND-ONLY: the weight vector is indexed by the enum and serialised, so the line goes last. Why it is worth more than a sink: state demand arrives in LUMPS and follows a weight a rival can lobby to move, so it is worth playing politics over rather than merely scaling into. ALSO OWNS spacecraft_components (BL-648's measurement, 2026-08-26): the guard's red list came back with ELEVEN goods, not the ten expected, and the eleventh is this one. Its exemption claimed BL-350 procurement, but procurement is a resource-agnostic TRANSFER between two corps' pools - it moves goods without consuming them, and admitting it as an injector would substantiate the entire roster at once. src/world contains no militia, and corp_ai.cpp says outright that the scorer does not emit those verbs today, so nothing automatic buys it. This line is its first real buyer.

items.author: Ben
items.title: Research consumes goods, not only credits
items.design: Ben, 2026-08-26: 'perhaps we could make research consume alternate goods as well'. Design written into RESEARCH.md. It gives the TOP of the production chain a buyer and turns the tech ladder into an economic decision rather than a free accumulator only time gates. Two properties: the basket is era-banded like every other, and a shortfall SLOWS research rather than voiding it (the same shape every goods draw takes). BLOCKED BY DESIGN on BL-619 (research system), which is a session with Ben - the rates, and whether the draw sits on the university or on the nation's budget lines, belong to that session rather than being settled ahead of it.

items.author: Ben
items.title: A battle consumes what it fires - conflict as a demand shock
items.design: The conflict demand channel (MARKETS.md section Demand channels). MEASURED: ordnance is priced at 43.00, near the top of the ancient roster, and its only draw is a per-head upkeep rate that BL-635's rescale took to 0.0035 - effectively nil. So the roster's most valuable military good has no buyer. THE WORK: a battle draws ordnance in proportion to what it commits, against the owner's pool, deterministically. WHY IT IS THE MOST INTERESTING OF THE EIGHT: it is the only channel that couples the game's two pillars - it makes Conflict move Trade, so a war somewhere else is a price signal here. OWED: this item writes its paragraph into MILITARY.md.

items.author: Ben
items.title: Tobacco, spices, coffee and furs get the buyer they were authored for
items.design: MEASURED: four endemic goods are on the roster, extractable, priced - and wanted by nothing at all, in any band. They pass the orphan check by naming 'mercantile demand', which BL-648 shows does not exist. THE WORK: a household demand that scales with WEALTH rather than headcount, flavoured by NATIONAL CHARACTER so different nations crave different luxuries. That asymmetry is the design, not a detail: it makes the trade route directional by construction - extract where it grows, sell where the money is - which is the most Trade-shaped channel of the eight and the one that most directly serves the pillar. Note it is also the first demand whose SIZE is a function of prosperity, so it rewards a player who has made somewhere rich.

items.title: Finish the dissolution walk - ground follows the firm, and hoist the duplicated HQ rule
items.author: Ben
items.design: Two loose ends the wave-2 review barrier found in BL-628, neither a defect today. (1) world::province_holder takes a CORP id via battle_system.cpp's field_held_by, and dissolve_into's inventory does not carry it. Entity ids are monotonic with no recycling, so a stale holder is inert rather than aliasing - but R4's wording is 'no dangling reference survives', and ground is PROPERTY, so it TRANSFERS. Now written into FINANCE.md's three-way rule, which also gained a fourth outcome, KEEP, for the historical record - history is not property and is never rewritten, which is the one place a reference to the erased corp survives on purpose. Extend the harness fixture to hold a province, since it currently never constructs one. (2) recompute_hq in corp_command.cpp DUPLICATES designate_hq/corp_home_body from corporation_generation.cpp, including kProjectedReachUnits = 2.5f - unavoidable at authoring because another slice owned that file in the same wave. Both have landed; the review verified them line-for-line identical. Hoist to a shared seam so they cannot drift.

items.title: charter_reach is computed at generation and silently zeroed on load
items.author: Ben
items.design: Found by the wave-2 review barrier. BL-638 added settlement_state::charter (a charter_reach), and w_settlement/r_settlement do not carry it. The omission is SYMMETRIC so the stream stays consistent and no version bump is owed - it is not a corruption bug. It is a LATENT one: the field is silently zeroed on load, which is benign only while the sole readers are generate_corporations and its harness, both of which run before any save exists. It becomes wrong the moment BL-627 (profitability ledger), BL-629 (rival acquisition) or the generation ledger reads charter off a LOADED world - and it will read as 'this world has no charter' rather than as an error. TWO HONEST ROUTES, pick one and say why: serialise it (a version bump, claimed through next_save_version.js), or RECOMPUTE it on load from the ladder it is derived from, which costs no format change and cannot drift from its source. The second is probably right, since charter_reach is a pure function of already-serialised state.

items.title: A demand injector that cannot price a basket entry must SAY SO, not skip it
items.author: Ben
items.design: THE MECHANISM THAT MADE TWO SEPARATE BUGS INVISIBLE ON THE SAME DAY, which is why it is an item rather than a note. inject_population_demand and inject_background_demand both SKIP a basket entry whose resource carries no market base price - silently, with no warning and no row anywhere. Consequences observed 2026-08-26: (1) BL-649's census read as having no background demand at all on its first run, and (2) tools/verify/spawn_solvency.cpp - whose own header says it loads world_gen.lua and did not - measured BL-635's entire spawn diagnosis in a world where background demand did not exist. Neither failed. Both just quietly answered a question about a different world. THE WORK: an injector that cannot price a basket entry must report it - a named diagnostic on the first occurrence, and a harness row that FAILS on a basket naming an unpriced good, since that combination is always either a missing script or an authoring error and is never intended. A basket entry is a STATEMENT that somebody wants the good; silently dropping it turns a design statement into a no-op. Cheap, and it protects every measurement the rest of Sprint 21 depends on.

items.title: The eighth field - a return sees the whole quarter, not just the money loop
items.author: Ben
items.design: Ben's ruling, 2026-08-26, on NR-655/NR-668 - option A of the three-way fork, and the measurement that forced it: a firm earning through mercenary contracts files a trailing_net IDENTICAL to a firm that earns nothing there, so BL-628's buyout undervalues it by exactly 640 credits (k 8.0 x the 80/quarter the record cannot see). Design in FINANCE.md section The eighth field. THE WORK: add `other` to quarterly_return = the whole-tick balance delta minus the money-loop net, and MOVE THE FILING from the end of apply_budget to after the tick's last balance mover - which is the part that needs care, since apply_budget does not own the tick and the headless harnesses call it directly. Then re-point corp_trailing_net at the mean of (net + other) so the buyout prices off the whole quarter. THREE PROPERTIES TO ASSERT: the seven flows still explain `net` unchanged; net+other telescopes EXACTLY over a run (the retain property extended from one function to the whole tick); and BL-628's own harness row that currently PINS the 640-credit blindness must be re-specified to pin the closure instead - do not delete it, invert it. `other` is deliberately NOT itemised: split into named lines it becomes a second budget breakdown competing with corp_budget, and the reason there is one accounting authority is that two of them disagree. Versions the save format.

items.title: A short pool buys on the market, up to a reservation ceiling
items.author: Ben
items.design: THE BLOCKER UNDER BL-641, AND PROBABLY UNDER FOUR MORE CHANNELS. Measured 2026-08-26: with building upkeep rates on, operating firms went 227 -> 19, because the goods drawn are produced 0.0 in band and a POOL DRAW never reaches market_component::demand - so the want never becomes a price, no rival scores the building that would supply it, and the sink starves itself. run_construction and run_processing already bid; run_unit_upkeep does not and carries the same latent defect. DESIGN-OWED, and the open question is Ben's because it widens FINANCE.md: should a goods draw place real demand on the market when the pool is short - and if so, does it BUY (spending credits, which makes upkeep a market participant) or merely SIGNAL (raising price without a transaction, which is cheaper but invents demand nobody pays for)? The first is coherent and expensive; the second is a thumb on the scale and should probably be refused on the same grounds the project refuses clamps. Until this is settled, BL-641's rates stay at 0.0 and every remaining channel (BL-643 infrastructure, BL-644 state, BL-645 research, BL-646 conflict) should be checked against property 3 before it is built, not after. SETTLED (Ben, 2026-08-26): 'Buy on the market, but at a threshold, buying is not allowed. This goes hand in hand with maximum and minimum prices for goods.' And ONE RULE FOR EVERY GOODS DRAW - unit upkeep takes the same shape, not a second one. Written into MARKETS.md section Settled: a short pool BUYS, up to a reservation ceiling. THE WORK: a short pool bids the shortfall into market_component::demand and pays for what it gets; above the ceiling it does not bid at all and the existing shortfall rule weakens the building (or unit) instead. The ceiling is authored in the PRICE BAND family beside floor_mult/ceil_mult, not in upkeep - it is a statement about what a good is worth paying, not about who is buying - and its value is MEASURED against the census and the operating-firm count, never guessed. It is the exact mirror of BL-386's seller-side floor_price: both sides may decline a trade, neither may dictate one. Turning BL-641's rates non-zero is gated on this landing.

items.title: Decide what actually shapes background density - the ratio, or the per-resource cap
items.author: Ben
items.design: Raised by BL-655's measurement and by its novelty flag. Pass 6 is documented as stopping on a 0.90 production/demand ratio, described as 'an emergent measurement rather than an injected clearing constant' and 'a stop condition, not a firm-count budget'. MEASURED: the ratio NEVER BINDS on the worlds we generate. `per_resource_firm_cap = 8` binds on every demanded resource, so the count is exactly specialists + 8 x basket breadth - which reproduced 104, 64 and 56 corps exactly across three configurations. Its own comment still says 'provisional - measure, then pin'. The doc has been corrected to describe what the code does; what is OPEN is which behaviour is wanted. THREE READINGS: (a) the cap is the real design and the ratio is dead weight - pin the cap deliberately, say density is breadth-driven, and delete the ratio; (b) the ratio is the real design and the cap is an emergency brake set too low - raise it until the ratio binds, which restores the 'calibrated, not authored' property the doc claims; (c) both, with the cap as a genuine guard against a pathological basket. Note the consequence either way: under (a) density becomes a function of how many DIFFERENT goods are wanted, so every demand channel Sprint 21 adds moves the world's size - which may be a feature.

items.title: A firm underwater long enough exits - give interest the consequence it is supposed to have
items.author: Ben
items.design: MEASURED 2026-08-26 from Ben's own observation of the live build. Of 12 seeds, 3 clear with ZERO interest; the 9 that fail all dipped negative once and interest is then 43-60% of their whole loss, against an operating gap of only -24 to -40 cr/qtr. 1.02^80 = 4.9x over the warm start. The rate is not the defect - components.hpp's 'no insolvency consequence' is. A firm that would have died in year three trades for twenty and is handed to the player as wreckage. THE WORK: a firm underwater for N consecutive quarters EXITS - dissolved, or absorbed via BL-628's dissolve_into, which already moves holdings, pools, balance and returns and cancels the promises nobody is left to keep. N and the trigger are authored in economy.lua and MEASURED, not picked. DESIGN-OWED on three questions that are Ben's: (1) dissolve or absorb - absorption by a solvent neighbour is richer and reuses the buyout path, dissolution is simpler and leaves ground free; (2) does this run IN PLAY as well as in the pre-game, i.e. can the player's own corp fail - NR-670 already ruled a rival may not BUY the player out, and this is a different question about the player failing on their own account; (3) what happens to the ground and the workforce - a dissolved firm's tiles should probably become available rather than stay held. EXPECTED CONSEQUENCE, and the reason this is priority A: the field at seat time becomes self-selected for viability, so BL-630's shortlist floor should start being met instead of falling through to its fallback on 23 of 24 seeds.

items.title: The solvency gate tests the price, not the position after the debt transfers
items.author: Ben
items.design: MEASURED by BL-634, which found it by taking its own brief's gate literally. The acquisition price is max(0, book_value + k x trailing_net + balance) and the balance term is SIGNED, so a deeply indebted firm's negative cash cancels its book value, the sum goes below zero, and the floor hands it over FREE. On 5 of 8 seeds the cheapest buyable firm cost exactly 0 cr. The dissolution rule then transfers the debt at face value: one seed took on -13,358 cr for nothing, and 3 of 8 buyers that bought the cheapest firm were sunk by it. THE FLOOR IS NOT THE BUG - a worthless firm is worth nothing, and NR-648's reasoning stands. The bug is that the SOLVENCY GATE READS THE PRICE rather than the buyer's balance AFTER the transfer, which is the same shape as the non-finite-price bug BL-628 caught in its own code: a check applied to the wrong quantity. THE WORK: gate on the post-acquisition position, so a corp cannot be handed a liability it could never have chosen to take on. Then re-run acquisition_viability's --target cheapest sweep, where 'still earning after' should go 5/8 -> 8/8. Note the harness already measures BOTH gates and its --target flag exists for exactly this comparison.

items.title: Population lens: regional heatmap with harder scaling, not a per-tile mark
items.design:
Ben, 2026-08-28: "Population: Let's see what this looks like as a heatmap with more extreme scaling. This way we should be able to see population regionally, not just on each tile."

Today the lens draws "per-tile value marks, workforce efficiency" (LENSES.md routing table) - a per-tile read, which is why a region of moderate population and a region of none look similar at whole-planet zoom. Two changes: a continuous heatmap fill rather than discrete marks, and a scaling curve steep enough that regional differences separate instead of compressing into the middle of the ramp.

EXPLICITLY AN EXPERIMENT, in Ben's own framing - "let's see what this looks like". The deliverable is a capture to rule on, not a settled design; expect a second pass on the curve. Worth measuring the actual population distribution first so the curve is fitted to the data rather than guessed - the same discipline BL-649's census brought to demand.

items.title: Scarcity lens: drop the dead Opportunity code, reuse its glyph, render market scarcity per resource
items.design:
Ben, 2026-08-28: "I support changing opportunity to scarcity. Drop the old code, reuse the glyph, and render market scarcity per resource."

READ AS: the lens KEEPS the name Scarcity - the earlier idea of renaming it to Opportunity is dropped - while the retired Opportunity lens's leftovers are deleted and its GLYPH is reused for Scarcity. Recorded explicitly because the instruction can be read in both directions, and because the session had just flagged that Opportunity is a name BL-604 retired; if this reading is wrong it is a one-line revert.

WHY A GLYPH MATTERS HERE: Scarcity is keyboard-cycle only, which is why Ben listed it among the lenses needing glyphs. icons::opportunity survives in src/ui/icons.{hpp,cpp} with no caller since BL-604, so the mark exists and is unused - reusing it costs nothing and lets Scarcity earn a strip slot, since LENSES.md's rule is that an on-screen lens carries one distinct glyph.

Also dead and worth removing in the same sweep, though Ben named only Opportunity: icons::country (BL-601) and icons::production (BL-604), neither of which has a caller.

The behaviour half - "render market scarcity per resource" - may already hold: the lens draws "per-market shortfall blocks + key" keyed to the selected resource, and the 2026-08-28 sweep captured scarcity_lens_full_iron and _steel. Confirm before changing anything; the glyph may be the whole of the real work.

items.title: Give every strip-eligible lens a distinct glyph (Company; Supply, Supply-routes, Reach deferred)
items.design:
Ben, 2026-08-28: "It looks like we need to add glyphs for scarcity, supply, supply-routes, and reach."

SCOPE NARROWED BY BEN THE SAME DAY: "I don't think we need body-to-body lenses yet. Keep the code but ignore for this session." Supply, Supply-routes and Reach are all body-to-body, so their glyphs are deferred with them - the code stays, the work waits. Scarcity is covered by BL-662 (it inherits the Opportunity mark).

WHAT REMAINS LIVE HERE IS THE COMPANY LENS, added 2026-08-28. It borrows icons::corporation while keyboard-only, on the precedent Reach and Supply-routes set. It cannot join the on-screen strip until it has its own mark, because Corp would be its immediate neighbour and LENSES.md forbids two strip neighbours sharing a glyph. A company is a background firm, so the mark wants to read as smaller/plural against the corporation's single solid form.

Three glyphs are dead and free to cannibalise: icons::country, icons::opportunity (claimed by BL-662), icons::production.

items.title: The labour read has no home, and wage competition is invisible
items.author: Claude
items.design:
FILED SO A FINDING IS NOT DELETED ALONG WITH THE SURFACE THAT DISPLAYED IT WRONGLY. BL-676 retires the Economy panel on Ben's 2026-08-29 call. Two of its three views were duplicates and one was a visibility breach, but the Workforce view was answering a real question badly rather than answering a redundant one - and after the deletion nothing answers it at all.

WHAT THE CAPTURE PASS MEASURED. The workforce table drew eighteen rows and every single one read "82% (labour short)". The panel's own doc had warned the mock fixture was uniform at 85% and said explicitly: verify against the live sim, not the CSV. Verified against the live sim - it is uniform there too.

AND IT IS NOT A BUG. `report.workforce_contention` is the POOL-LEVEL min(1, supply/demand) keyed (corp, body), and every corp in the fixture holds on one body, so one pool yields one number correctly repeated eighteen times. The view is not broken; it is showing a quantity that cannot vary in the situation it is shown in.

THE ACTUAL FINDING: BL-614 (wage competition) SUPERSEDED that scalar and nothing surfaces what replaced it. economy_system.cpp says so in terms - when a pool is contended the uniform proportional scalar no longer applies; scarce labour allocates building by building, offered wage descending (base_wage x (1 + wage_bid)), building id ascending on a tie, each granted up to its demand until the pool is spent. The marginal building takes a partial grant and those below it get nothing. The factor a building actually runs at is `report.building_labour[id]`, and the pool aggregate survives only as a reporting figure.

So there is a real mechanic here - bidding for scarce labour, and losing a building's shift to a rival who bid higher - and the only surface that ever mentioned labour rendered it as one number eighteen times. `building_labour[id]` is per building and varies; it is the quantity a player would act on.

DESIGN-OWED, AND DELIBERATELY NOT SCOPED HERE. Where this lives is open and is Ben's: a section on the building Selection card (per-building, where the number's grain actually is), a view on the Corporation dashboard beside the existing Workforce roll-up card, or a surface of its own. What is settled is only that it has no home today and that the Budget ledger's Wages tier currently has no visible consequence anywhere.

items.title: A top-bar tracker for the quantities that gate progression - level and rate, e.g. "200 Steel (+25/qtr)"
items.author: Ben
items.design:
Ben, 2026-08-30: "a tracker for important items on the top-nav bar. We should show a stockpile for steel, a new type or resource (boost), which is untradeable, and research points. These can all have an absolute value for how much is in stockpile, and an addition to the right. E.g. '200 Steel (+25/qtr)'."

THE READ IT ADDS. The header today answers "how is my money" - BALANCE, STOCKPILE (one aggregated credit figure), NET/qtr and RUNWAY. It answers nothing about the GOODS a player is accumulating, so the three quantities that gate progression are invisible unless a ledger is opened. The tracker is the always-on half of that: a level and its rate, in the shape the header already uses for money.

THE FORMAT IS BEN'S AND IS THE WHOLE SPEC: `200 Steel (+25/qtr)` - absolute stockpile, name, and the per-quarter delta to its right. The delta is the same quantity the header's NET already reports for credits, so the two read as one family rather than two conventions.

TWO OF THE THREE QUANTITIES DO NOT EXIST, and that is the item's real shape - it is a design item before it is a UI one. Do not start with the header.
  1. STEEL exists. It is an Industrial-tier resource with a live recipe chain, so its stockpile and its per-quarter movement are both readable today. This third is buildable now and is the one that proves the format.
  2. BOOST DOES NOT EXIST, and neither does untradeability. `RESOURCES.md` owns the roster and has no such resource; more importantly the model has no UNTRADEABLE PROPERTY - the nearest thing is a market opening at all-zero base_price, which is an accident of a fixture rather than a declared rule (`market_clearing.hpp`). An untradeable good is a genuinely new kind of thing: it cannot be bought, so the only way to have it is to make it, which makes it a different lever from every resource now in the game. That needs Ben's design, not an implementer's guess - what produces Boost, what consumes it, and what untradeable means at the order book (refused listing? absent from the goods table? present at no price?).
  3. RESEARCH POINTS DO NOT EXIST either - grep finds no research_point quantity anywhere in `src/world`. `RESEARCH.md` is a stub and BL-619 (RESEARCH_SYSTEM) is an open DESIGN SESSION WITH BEN, not a build slice. This third is gated on that item and must not be faked with a placeholder number.

SO THE ITEM SPLITS THREE WAYS, and only the first can start: build the tracker with Steel and a shape that takes N entries; add Boost when its design lands; add research points when BL-619 does. A header that shows one tracker is honest; one that shows three where two are zeros is not.

WHERE IT LIVES. `docs/ui/HEADER.md` owns the top bar and is the authority for the surface. `docs/economy/RESOURCES.md` owns Boost and the untradeable property. `docs/economy/RESEARCH.md` and BL-619 own research points. The header is fixed chrome on every frame, so its cost is paid always - `LAYOUT.md`'s constraint, and the reason the entry count is a design question rather than a free parameter.

CARRIED OUT OF A RETIRED SPRINT. This was the shell-chrome batch's subject (old sprint 25), which Ben deleted on 2026-08-30 as not needing a revisit. This is the one piece he kept, so it rides in sprint 25 (canvases) despite being header-grain.

items.title: Spectator mode is reachable from the running game, not only from a --verify script
items.author: Ben
items.design:
Ben, 2026-08-31: "hopefully by the end of this sprint we can use a spectator mode to view AI playing in real time, and tighten core gameplay loops." This item is the route that makes that sentence possible; every other item in the sprint is watched THROUGH it.

THE GAP, MEASURED. `ui_state::spectating` has exactly ONE assignment site in the whole tree: `verify.spectate(on)` at src/core/verify_api.cpp:1096, bound behind --verify. There is no CLI flag and no in-game control. So spectate is today a headless-script capability only - the mode exists, is carried through to `corp_ai_params::spectating`, has a determinism harness guarding it (tools/verify/spectator_determinism.cpp), and cannot be entered by a person sitting in front of the game.

WHAT IT NEEDS. A route in, and honest behaviour once in. Two halves:
  1. ENTRY. A --spectate CLI flag is the cheap half and pairs with the existing --autostart family in main.cpp. Whether it ALSO wants a menu / new-game control is the design question - STARTUP.md owns the screen state machine, and a mode chosen at world creation is a different thing from one toggled mid-session. Toggling mid-session is the harder claim: BL-409's grant is written as a property of the SESSION (nobody seated), and flipping it live changes who the scorer may act on halfway through a run. Prefer entry-at-start unless mid-session toggling is separately argued.
  2. THE VIEW. `god_view` is the second flag and is the one that makes watching worth doing - it lifts the survey mask and opens rival internals (BL-408; read sites in body_surface_canvas.cpp, hover_content.cpp, selection_panel.cpp). It is gated on the PAIR `spectating && god_view` at every read site, so it is already safe; it needs its own control, offered only while spectating - time_panel.cpp:344-350 already has the shape.

DETERMINISM IS THE CONSTRAINT AND IT IS ALREADY PAID FOR. spectator_determinism.cpp asserts the two properties the standing rule names - the flag DEFAULTS FALSE so an ordinary played session is byte-identical, and admitting one more corp shifts no rival's cadence slot. Adding a route must not touch either. Re-run that harness as the verification, and do not re-bless its constant to make a change fit.

ACTIONS.json: any new control gets its entry, per the standing rule that a control change updates the dictionary.

items.title: The AI decision feed reports the real chosen candidate and its score, not 'overridden' at 0.00 on every row
items.author: Ben
items.design:
Raised as NR-626: every row in the AI decision feed reads 'overridden' with a chosen score of 0.00.

WHY IT IS FIRST AND NOT COSMETIC. The feed is the only window onto rival reasoning, and this sprint's whole method is WATCHING the AI and tightening from what is seen. A readout that prints the same thing on every row cannot distinguish a working scorer from a broken one - so every later item in this sprint would be tuned blind through it. It is the instrument, and the instrument is reading zero.

IT IS ALSO THE SURFACE THE NEW GOAL DEPENDS ON. AI_OPPONENT.md § The goal makes restraint a first-class move and calls the AI 'transparent by construction' on the strength of the decision log carrying a restrained move's REASON. A held move that prints as 'overridden, 0.00' is indistinguishable from a stall. Restraint that cannot be read looks exactly like incompetence, which is the failure mode the legibility requirement exists to prevent.

SCOPE. Find why the chosen candidate is not reaching the feed - whether the score is not carried out of the scorer, or is carried and not rendered - and fix it at the cause. `corp_decision_reason` already has a named-reason vocabulary (corp_ai.cpp ~line 285 renders 'workforce margin', 'recipe margin' and siblings), so the words largely exist; the question is why the feed is not receiving them.

OUT OF SCOPE: adding the 'held: already ahead' reason itself, which arrives with the margin term (BL-698, scorer margin term) and needs this fixed first to be visible at all.

items.title: The AI skill harness bands the spread in composite standing across the field, not absolute net worth
items.author: Ben
items.design:
AI_OPPONENT.md § The goal now makes a CLOSE RACE the intended shape of a campaign, produced by the world's brakes rather than by any agent's restraint. The instrument that scores the AI cannot see that quantity at all.

WHAT THE HARNESS MEASURES TODAY. Four per-seed metrics against golden bands: the net-worth curve (summed non-player balances), solvency ticks, survival fraction, and per-verb action counts. All four are absolute or aggregate. None can tell a run where every corp grew together from a run where one corp ran away - both sit inside a generous summed-net-worth band, and only the second is now a failure.

THE METRIC TO ADD. The spread between the leading corporation and the field, sampled on the existing SAMPLE_EVERY cadence. Held narrow is the pass; a widening gap is the regression. Exact form is the design call - leader-over-median and leader-over-second are both defensible, and the choice should be made against a real run's numbers rather than picked first (Rule 0b: report the observed spread with units, then choose).

THE ABSOLUTE BANDS DO NOT GO. They demote to a SOLVENCY FLOOR underneath the margin band. A world where the margin is beautifully narrow because every corp is broke is not a pass, and only the absolute figures can catch that.

CARRIED DEBT, and it belongs to whoever takes this item (NR-305): the current bands were blessed 2026-08-16 and are stale against everything since - possibly the mercenary contracts, the nation grants, or the roster widening. Re-derive from a fresh bless with dated provenance in the harness's own provenance-log idiom. Goldens here are disposable by project convention; the provenance comment is not.

ORDERING: this lands BEFORE BL-698 (scorer margin term). Building the objective before the measurement means tuning blind.

RETARGETED 2026-08-31 by Ben's systemic ruling. Two changes from the item as first minted:
  1. The banded quantity is the spread in COMPOSITE STANDING (BL-700, composite standing index), not in cash. Balance alone misreads the game constantly - a corp that just spent its treasury on a smelter is not behind.
  2. It is measuring whether THE WORLD'S BRAKES WORK, not whether an agent obeyed an instruction. No actor aims at the margin, so a widening spread is a finding about coalitions and climate, not about the scorer.

BEN'S FIRST-CUT TARGET, 2026-08-31: a leader roughly 28% ahead of the field. Treat that as the band to aim the SYSTEM at, not as a parameter to set anywhere - nothing in the code should know the number.

items.title: An opt-in margin dial scales a leading corp's whole candidate set - the difficulty knob, not the foundation
items.author: Ben
items.design:
DEMOTED 2026-08-31, the same day it was minted, by Ben's systemic ruling (AI_OPPONENT.md § Where restraint comes from). It was the sprint's centrepiece for about an hour. Read that section before this item - the demotion IS the design.

BEN'S OBJECTION, and it is correct: "The angle we are taking here is a literal handicap. I prefer to consider it as always a force from within the game system." A term in the scorer that says 'ease off, I am ahead' is invisible, uncausable and uncounterable. The player cannot see it, provoke it, benefit from it or fight it. It also buys its slim margin by making the AI worse, which § The goal forbids.

SO THIS IS NO LONGER HOW RESTRAINT HAPPENS. Coalitions (BL-699, rival coalitions) and climate (BL-701, living climate) are the foundation. This item survives ONLY as the explicit, opt-in DIFFICULTY KNOB Ben kept - "we can keep both modes" - and it is named as one, in the § 1 Area 4 sense of a small transparent economic handicap.

TWO HARD CONSTRAINTS, both from Ben, 2026-08-31.
  1. EVEN SCALING ACROSS EVERY CANDIDATE. Not a carve-out that discounts expansion and spares efficiency. Ben chose the even form deliberately over the surgical one.
  2. IT MAY NEVER VETO CONSTRUCTION OR EXTENSION. "'how far restraint goes' should never exclude extension and construction. If a player loses out, they should be able to see that the world doesn't wait for them." A dialled-down corp still builds, just less. A brake that freezes a leader destroys the honest consequence of falling behind, which is the thing the whole design protects.

OFF BY DEFAULT. The systemic route must be able to produce a close race on its own; if this dial is needed to get one, the brakes are the thing to fix. Ships as a mode, not as a default, and the harness bands the DEFAULT world.

Measured today for the record: corp_ai.cpp scores purely absolutely, and the only mention of `world::player_entity` is to EXCLUDE the player's corp (corp_ai.cpp:566-574, 625). Tunables live in corp_ai_params, per that file's own convention.

items.title: Rivals score stance against composite standing, so coalitions form against whoever leads
items.author: Ben
items.design:
PROMOTED 2026-08-31 from a nice-to-have to THE PRIMARY BRAKE. Ben: "With 7 corporations, we have plenty of room for alliances to form against leaders... I prefer if an agent's decision to slow down can be framed as usually motivated by systems." AI_OPPONENT.md § Where restraint comes from is the authority.

THE SHAPE. A rival's stance scoring reads WHO IS WINNING - the composite standing index from BL-700 (composite standing index). A corp near the top of the field attracts hostility; corps below it find each other worth befriending. The brake is applied TO the leader BY others, and no corp ever throttles itself. Every corporation keeps playing flat out; leading simply becomes expensive.

WHY THIS IS BETTER THAN A SCORER TERM, and why it is worth the extra difficulty: a coalition has a CAUSE, it is VISIBLE, and the player can join it, split it, provoke it or be its target. It converts the brake into gameplay. It also satisfies the standing rule that every system justify itself by feeding Trade or Conflict - a margin term feeds neither; a coalition feeds both.

THE VERBS ALREADY EXIST AND ARE UNUSED. corp_command.hpp carries four stance verbs from BL-448 - declare_hostile, offer_friendship, accept_friendship, return_to_neutral - specified, validated and serialised. corp_ai.cpp names NONE of them, so every rival is permanently neutral by omission rather than by choice. This item is the scoring that issues them; no new verb is needed.

THE PERMISSION EXISTS AND IS DATED. io-standing-rules.md carries Ben's 2026-08-22 grant for a rival scoring stance toward the player's corp, on the BL-450 terms - deterministic, seeded, scored-utility, legal verbs only, never a planner - and records that hostility stays a DECLARED state a corp opts into, never acquired ambiently. NOTE the provenance: BL-450 was PURGED in the 2026-08-23 cull, not completed; its prose is REFERENCE ONLY and this is authored fresh, per the cull's own resurrection rule.

THE COALITION MUST BE LEGIBLE OR IT IS JUST A HIDDEN HANDICAP AGAIN. That is the whole point of the reframe, so it is a requirement of this item and not a follow-up: a stance change emits into the § 7 chat channel and the decision feed, with its reason. A player must be able to SEE that the field has turned on the leader - and, when the leader is them, see it coming.

MUST NOT VETO EXTENSION (Ben, 2026-08-31). Coalition pressure makes leading costly; it never stops a corp building. See § The constraint on restraint.

OUT OF SCOPE: lobbying (nation-grain, purged as BL-539, unowned - NR-744), nation stance gating the player (BL-540, likewise), and the Stage C dialogue layer (BL-334, likewise).

items.title: A corporation's standing is a composite of economic, research and military power
items.author: Ben
items.design:
Ben, 2026-08-31, asked what quantity the margin is measured in: "It should be an aggregate of net worth, research, military strength... Maybe others too." AI_OPPONENT.md § Standing is the authority.

THE PREREQUISITE FOR TWO ITEMS, which is why it is minted separately: BL-699 (rival coalitions) scores stance against it, and BL-697 (skill harness margin metric) bands its spread. Both need the same number and must not each invent one.

ALL THREE COMPONENTS EXIST TODAY. Verified 2026-08-31 by reading the tree, because the backlog prose elsewhere claims research does not:
  * ECONOMIC - net worth: balance plus the assessed value of buildings and held stock.
  * RESEARCH - `science`, the corp research accumulator (BL-332, components.hpp:1343). Stockpiled, market-invisible, never decaying; REACHED, not spent. Already readable as a condition_set value (condition_set.hpp:77).
  * MILITARY - summed `unit_strength(world, unit_component)` over the corp's fielded units. COMPUTED, not stored: BL-459 removed the stored `strength` field in 2026-08-17, so read the function, never a field.

NOTE 'maybe others too' IS DELIBERATELY LEFT OPEN by Ben. Build the aggregate so a fourth component is an addition rather than a rewrite - the weighting is data, and territory or market share are the obvious candidates if the composite reads wrong when watched.

WHY NOT BALANCE ALONE, which is what everything measures today: a corp that has just spent its treasury on a smelter is not behind, and a corp hoarding cash while its rivals arm is not ahead. A cash-only index would have coalitions forming against the wrong corporation, which is the failure mode hardest to notice because it still looks like diplomacy.

DETERMINISM. Read at a settled point in the tick and stable under the sorted-corp iteration order, or the evaluation cadence becomes the tiebreak. Name the read point explicitly and assert it - the standing rule's constraint on every scorer input.

WEIGHTS IN corp_ai_params, per that file's convention. Expect to tune them by watching (BL-695, live spectate route), not on paper.

items.title: Climate is designed and documented as the NEXT Era's catastrophe, outside prototype scope
items.author: Ben
items.design:
DOCUMENTATION ONLY, per Ben 2026-08-31: "Move BL-701 to just documentation - it's not the focus here." Filed the same day at difficulty 8 as a system build; it is not that, and nothing here builds climate.

IT TOOK THREE PASSES IN ONE SESSION AND THE CORRECTIONS ARE THE VALUE. Recorded so the reasoning is not re-derived:

PASS 1 proposed running climate through `tile_component.hazard_level` - static (written once at tile_generation.cpp:1962), already carried by the production formula's (1 - hazard) multiplier. REJECTED by Ben: "we will use a more detailed surface than hazard. Hazard is mostly just a tangible benefit for larger settlements on other bodies." One number per tile with one meaning cannot carry a body-scale state with several.

PASS 2 found the right surface - `planetology_state` unfrozen. Io already runs a physically grounded climate model at generation (the carbonate-silicate thermostat, the greenhouse budget, insolation, oxygenation, the arable calculation) and freezes the result. Climate change is a defined subset of those scalars moving: instellation, surface_temp_k, arable_share, life_stage, o2_fraction slowly. Fixed: endowment and the planetary facts. THIS SURVIVES. The dividing line is that climate moves what a world can SUPPORT, never what it is MADE OF.

PASS 2 ALSO got the era placement wrong, treating the nuclear war as a scheduled boundary event and climate as its aftermath. REJECTED by Ben: "The aim of each era is to give a catastrophe for players to avoid... I am not against climate change being a large problem for Era 2, but our prototype works solely on Era 1 for now."

PASS 3, WHICH STANDS. Every Era carries ONE CATASTROPHE THE PLAYER PLAYS TO AVOID, resolved deterministically from a watched scalar. The prototype Era's catastrophe is a nuclear war and its scalar is ALARM. Climate is the NEXT Era's catastrophe and its scalar is LOAD. CLIMATE.md is now written as that parallel, so the machinery built for the first rung - watched scalar, seeded test, red herrings with tells, deed-gated capstones - is what the second rung reuses. That parallel is what makes the Era ladder a system rather than a series of set-pieces.

THE ERA MODEL ITSELF WAS PROMOTED OUT OF RESEARCH in the same pass. ERAS.md § The point of an Era now carries the Ceiling/Alarm model, the test, the seven red-herring kinds, the tell-before-commitment rule and the inverse herring - drafted 2026-08-05 in docs/research/ERA1_TECH_LANDSCAPE.md and owned by BL-087, which the 2026-08-23 cull PURGED. The design was sitting in a research doc that is explicitly not authority. See NR-750.

KNOCK-ON, and it is the one that changes another design: AI_OPPONENT.md had named climate as the SECOND systemic brake on a runaway leader. Climate is out of prototype scope, so coalitions now carry that brake ALONE, and the doc says so plainly rather than leaning on an unavailable system.

items.title: God view has a control under spectate - ALREADY DELIVERED by BL-408, closed unbuilt
items.author: Ben
items.design:
CLOSED 2026-08-31 WITHOUT A LINE OF CODE. The item's premise was wrong and the control already existed.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE, on main before this sprint: `src/ui/time_panel.cpp:353` carries `ImGui::Checkbox("God view", &st.god_view)` inside an `if (st.spectating)` block, landed by BL-408 in commit 701cba55. It has its `chrome.sysmenu_god_view` ACTIONS entry, its `god_view_toggle` question-log entry, a `ui_elements.json` entry, and a visual check at `scripts/verify/spectator_god_view.lua`. Offered only while spectating, and a checkbox is a toggle by construction. Every requirement this item wrote was already met.

HOW THE ITEM WAS FILED WRONG, recorded because the mistake is reusable. The claim was "god_view is written in exactly one place, verify_api.cpp:1103". That came from grepping for `god_view\s*=` — an ASSIGNMENT. ImGui writes through a pointer: `&st.god_view`. So the grep was structurally incapable of finding the real control, and the absence it reported was an absence of a syntax, not of a feature.

THE LESSON, and it generalises past this item: a grep for `x =` does not find writes to x. For a C++ codebase specifically it misses address-of arguments, references, and member functions that mutate. Where the question is "does anything set this", the honest checks are the address-of form and the type's mutating surface, or a look at the one file most likely to own the control.

The slice agent found this in minutes by reading time_panel.cpp rather than trusting the brief, which is the behaviour the sub-agent discipline is meant to produce.

items.title: A watched run produces a written finding on how the AI actually strategises, into STRATEGIES.md
items.author: Ben
items.design:
Ben, 2026-08-31: "Our aim for sprint 26 is to ensure spectator mode works, and visibly watch AI play in order to further develop the meta." THIS IS THE ITEM THAT DELIVERS THE SECOND HALF OF THAT SENTENCE, and it is the reason the sprint is not just plumbing.

WITHOUT IT THE SPRINT CAN END WITH A WORKING SPECTATE MODE AND NOTHING LEARNED. That is the specific failure this item exists to prevent: three instrument items land, everything is green, and no statement about rival play is any truer than it was at the start.

THE DELIVERABLE IS PROSE, NOT CODE. A run watched end to end on the 1960s start (BL-705, selectable 1960s start), with god view on, and a written finding: what the rivals actually did, in what order, what they never did, where the scorer looked competent and where it looked blind.

IT LANDS IN docs/ai/STRATEGIES.md, which owns the meta and was AUTHORED AHEAD OF THE GAME - CLAUDE.md calls it "the meta, authored ahead of the game - research, not authority". This is the first chance to check that authored meta against what the scorer actually does. TREAT A DIVERGENCE AS A FINDING ABOUT ONE OR THE OTHER, not as a defect in the scorer by default: an authored strategy that no rival ever reaches may be a scorer gap OR a meta that was never real.

WHAT TO LOOK FOR, so the watching has a spine rather than being a vibe:
  1. Does any rival do anything that reads as a PLAN across ticks, or only locally good moves?
  2. What does the field's spread in composite standing (BL-700) do over the run - converge, hold, or run away?
  3. Which corp_verbs are never issued? A verb family with zero uses across a run is either dead code or an unreachable candidate.
  4. What does the decision feed's reason vocabulary actually say, once BL-696 makes it say anything?
  5. Where does a rival do something a human would obviously not do? That is the legibility bar from AI_OPPONENT.md § The goal.

FILE WHAT IT FINDS as NEEDS_REVIEW entries and, where warranted, fresh items - do not fold defects into this item's own prose and call it done.

items.title: A run exports a per-rival trace of what was decided and why, so a finding can cite evidence
items.author: Ben
items.design:
Ben, 2026-08-31, approving the proposal. Optional relative to the sprint's core - BL-703 (watch session finding) can be done by watching alone - but it is what turns a finding from a memory of watching into something that cites evidence.

THE SHAPE: a per-run, per-corp log of the scorer's decisions - the candidate chosen, its score, the runners-up, the reason, the tick. The data already exists inside the evaluation; nothing new is computed, it is a question of getting it OUT in a form that can be read after the run rather than only watched during it.

THE ADJACENT MACHINERY IS ALREADY THERE and should be reused rather than duplicated: `corp_decision_reason` is the reason vocabulary; the decision feed consumes the same stream; AI_OPPONENT.md § 8a's world history log (history_log.{hpp,cpp}) is the project's append-only tagged serialisation seam and already carries a `decision` topic. Check whether this is a NEW export or a READER over the log that already exists - the second is much the better answer if it holds.

DETERMINISM: the trace is an OBSERVATION, never an input. Nothing in the scorer may read it, and its presence or absence must not change a single decision - assert that a run with tracing on and one with it off produce the same state_hash.

IT ALSO PAYS FORWARD. AI_OPPONENT.md § 10d's corpus-generation direction is exactly this artifact: "every decision is logged as an input/output pair... those pairs are the supervised fine-tuning corpus", and § 10d notes the corpus and the replay log are the same artifact. Do not build the corpus here - but do not build something that cannot become it.

items.title: The 1960s start is selectable, and the campaign epoch reads world_params instead of a hard-coded constant
items.author: Ben
items.design:
Ben, 2026-08-31: "We will be working on the 1960s start." This is what makes that sentence executable. Sprint 26 watches the AI play, and BL-703 (watch session finding) watches it on a 1960s world - which cannot currently be started.

THE BRANCH IS ALIVE AND UNREACHABLE, measured 2026-08-31. `world_params::epoch_year` defaults to 0 and its own comment says the 1960 arc is deliberately kept working: "pass epoch_year = 1960 and it still runs, which is what keeps the parked space work buildable". The branch is real - `era_band_for_epoch` puts the recipe registry on the industrial band, `era_minus_one.cpp` skips the antiquity prehistory above 1700, and hard_coded_world.cpp branches on the same threshold. But NOTHING EVER SETS IT. There is no CLI flag, no wizard field, and no assignment anywhere in src/. Reaching 1960 today means editing a default.

THE SECOND HALF IS A REAL BUG AND THIS ITEM INHERITS IT (raised earlier as the epoch half of the two-clocks entry). `campaign_epoch_year` is a hard-coded 1960 in BOTH src/ui/format.hpp:82 and src/world/planetology.hpp:275, tied by a static_assert in tile_inspector.cpp, and format.cpp:134 computes the displayed year as day_tick/days_per_year + that constant. NO UI SITE READS world_params::epoch_year AT ALL. So today a 0 CE campaign renders 1960-based dates - the constant is simply wrong for the default start.

NOTE THE POLARITY, because it decides the order of work: moving to a 1960s start makes the hard-coded constant ACCIDENTALLY CORRECT again. That is a trap. Fix the constant to read world_params anyway - a value that is right by coincidence will silently break the moment either start is used again, and both starts remain supported (ERAS.md § Where the ladder starts).

SCOPE:
  1. epoch_year is selectable - the wizard is the natural home (STARTUP.md owns the screen state machine); a CLI flag is the cheap first cut and pairs with the --autostart family.
  2. The UI epoch reads world_params rather than a constant, and the static_assert is replaced by whatever keeps the two clocks honest once the value is dynamic.
  3. Whatever is stale on the 1960 path gets found by walking it - this is the first time anyone has.

EXPECT TO FIND THINGS. The 0 CE start has had months of attention and the 1960 path has had none since the arc split. Treat surprises as findings to file, not as scope creep to absorb.
